# Rainfall over the upper Niger and Bani

CHIRPS v2 final monthly gridded estimates combine gauge information and infrared satellite observations. The native 0.05° grids are independent of SWOT. The window covers July to September, the principal rainy season preceding the annual flood. Each monthly value, source URL, compressed-byte count and SHA-256 is in `chirps_monthly.csv`. The yearly file sums three basin-mean months in millimetres. [CHIRPS](https://www.chc.ucsb.edu/data/chirps) · [Archived TIFs](https://data.chc.ucsb.edu/products/CHIRPS/v2.0/africa_monthly/tifs/)

The fixed mask contains all 51 HydroBASINS Africa v1c level-6 polygons draining through the outlet of HYBAS_ID 1060603890, which contains the center of Mopti reach 14279000471. Their database areas total 303,668.9 km². The basin outlet and the SWOT reach midpoint occupy different locations in the terminal polygon. The alternative series removes the entire terminal polygon (28,366.8 km²). The GeoJSON uses 0.001° simplification tolerance and four decimals. `basin_sources.json` records the exact point, upstream topology and geometry queries. HydroBASINS was developed by WWF and collaborators. [HydroBASINS](https://www.hydrosheds.org/products/hydrobasins) · [HydroBASINS v1c mirror](https://services.arcgis.com/hRUr1F8lE8Jq2uJo/arcgis/rest/services/HydroBASINS_Level6/FeatureServer)

Run `python3 chirps.py` with GDAL and NumPy. The script identifies pixels whose centres are inside the mask, weights them by the cosine of latitude and sums July–September means. The 1991–2020 mean is 727.07 mm. Totals are 651.16 mm in 2023, 871.90 mm in 2024 and 710.27 mm in 2025. The 2024 total ranks first among 35 seasons (1991–2025), 19.92% above the 30-year mean. Excluding the terminal polygon gives 915.17 mm, also first and 19.87% above its corresponding mean. These ranks describe the supplied period. They provide hydrometeorological context without identifying the hydraulic cause of a reach-scale anomaly.
